paragraphs.body: The Early Train

Usually, the professor lets us out right when class is over. By the time I get to the train station, I can catch the 5 o’clock train. The ride is about an hour long, and it’s always the same group of people, faces I recognize but don’t know.

annotations.comment: Tiny bit confusing in wording — maybe “when class is supposed to end” or something like that.

annotations.model_comment: The opening paragraph sets the scene for the train ride, but it lacks a clear conflict or goal for the main character. Consider adding an element of unexpected change or obstacle that the character must confront or overcome during the train ride. This will help to create a more engaging and dynamic story. For example, the professor letting the class out early could be the catalyst for an unexpected encounter or situation that the character must navigate.

paragraphs.body: But today was different, the professor let us out 45 minutes early which is weird because the syllabus literally said that would never happen.

annotations.comment: I like this title and the opening — you put me right into the story and told me a lot about the character immediately. It could work a little harder: “Usually, my bio professor lets us out early…” tells me a little more, for example.

annotations.model_comment: The opening of your paragraph sets up an unexpected event - the professor letting class out early. However, it would be more effective if you explicitly stated the conflict this event creates for your character. For example, you could mention how this early release puts your character in a time crunch to catch the earlier train, and how missing it would negatively impact their plans. This would establish the desire your character has and the opposition they face, which is essential for a compelling flash fiction piece.

paragraphs.body: I packed up my things, a little stunned. I could definitely make the earlier train. With a burst of energy from my Red Bull and the help of my trusty New Balances, I ran all the way to the station.

annotations.comment: Ah, the joy of a class getting out early!
annotations.context_left: l and the help of my

annotations.model_comment: The opening paragraph sets the scene for the protagonist's unexpected early release from class and her subsequent rush to catch the earlier train. However, it lacks a clear conflict or obstacle that the protagonist must overcome. To strengthen the paragraph, consider introducing an element that creates tension or resistance for the protagonist, such as a train that is about to depart or a competing character vying for the same seat. This will help establish the conflict and propel the story forward.

paragraphs.body: I don’t recognize these people and by the looks of it, it looks like its going to be a full train ride. So I hurry in and find an open seat. I’m still trying to catch my breath a little from my run here so I reach for my water bottle.

annotations.comment: I really like how you’re showing that the simplest change can really affect a life.

annotations.model_comment: The opening paragraph focuses on the protagonist's routine of catching the train after class. While the details are engaging, they don't introduce any significant conflict or tension. To make the opening more compelling, consider introducing an unexpected event or obstacle that forces the protagonist to act or adapt. For example, the professor letting the class out early could be an opportunity for the protagonist to encounter a new person or situation, leading to the development of the conflict.

paragraphs.body: “Mind if I sit here?”

I looked up and saw a tall man standing next to me. I didn’t recognize him, which was surprising considering my college campus has about only 2,000 students. Then again, this wasn’t my usual train. I nodded, still a bit out of breath, and took a sip of my water.

annotations.comment: I was a little surprised that such a small college has its own stop, but maybe this is in NYC or similar?

annotations.model_comment: The opening paragraph sets the scene for the encounter between the protagonist and the man on the train, but it could benefit from more detail to establish the conflict and create a sense of urgency. Consider adding specific details about the man's appearance or behavior that make the protagonist curious or intrigued, and include more description of her own thoughts and feelings to show her motivation for starting a conversation. Additionally, consider adding a clear obstacle or challenge that the protagonist must overcome in order to initiate the conversation, such as her nervousness or uncertainty. By establishing a clear conflict and setting the stage for the rest of the story, the opening paragraph will be more engaging and effective in drawing the reader in.

paragraphs.body: As he gets situated, I pull out a book I’m reading and that’s when I smelled it—a warm, inviting scent. Not too strong, not too weak. Just right. I always smell the men’s colognes when i’m at ULTA because they smell so good, so I recognized it when I smelt it. Ralph Laurens ralphs club. I hadn’t even talked to this man yet and I can just tell he has good taste.

annotations.model_comment: The description of the man's cologne and the recognition of the scent is an effective way to introduce the character's good taste and create intrigue. However, the paragraph could benefit from more focus on the conflict or the character's desire. For example, you could describe how the character is trying to start a conversation with the man or how she is nervous about approaching him. This would add tension and create a stronger sense of conflict, driving the story forward.

paragraphs.body: I pretended to look out the window, sneaking a glance. Light blue eyes, like the sky, and a clean-shaven face. Wow. Fate must have been on my side today—I get out of class early and end up next to this ridiculously handsome guy.

annotations.comment: Can you make it clear that earlier she doesn’t really even look at him?

annotations.model_comment: The opening of your paragraph is engaging, but it would benefit from more detail to help the reader visualize the scene and the character. Consider adding sensory details to bring the setting and the character to life. For example, you could describe the color of the man's eyes in more detail, or mention the sound of the train or the feel of the seat beneath the character. This will help the reader connect with the character and the setting, and create a stronger foundation for the rest of the story.

paragraphs.body: I hadn’t talked to anyone new since freshman year, and now I am a junior. Plus, my New Year’s resolution was to put myself out there more. This was my chance. What could go wrong?

annotations.comment: I like the slow introduction here of what she wants — you could perhaps introduce the idea that she’s a loner or shy earlier? She doesn’t chat with anyone in the classroom, perhaps?

paragraphs.body: But how was I going to do it? I could compliment his cologne, but I didn’t want him to think I was weirdly sniffing him. He was also reading a book—I could ask him about it.

I started getting nervous as the minutes ticked by. What if he got off at the next stop? I decided to create a diversion. I bent down to my bag, planning to “accidentally” drop something to start a conversation. Just as I was about to, the train slammed on the brakes. Hard. I was thrown forward, bracing for impact with the floor.
But then, a hand grabbed my arm, catching me before I could fall. My heart skipped a beat. I looked up to see him holding onto me, his face full of concern.
“Are you alright?”

I felt my cheeks flush with embarrassment. I just look at him with a smile hoping he didn’t notice the blush creeping up my face. We both looked up as the PA system crackled, “Sorry for the inconvenience folks, there will be a delay due to an obstruction on the tracks.”

annotations.model_comment: Consider introducing a clearer conflict or obstacle for the protagonist in this scene. This could be another passenger trying to take the seat, a delay in the train causing her to miss an important appointment, or an unexpected encounter with someone from her past. By establishing a clearer conflict, the scene will have more tension and direction, and the reader will be more invested in the protagonist's experience.

paragraphs.body: Great. I got on the early train, and now I wouldn’t get home any sooner. But then again, it meant more time next to train guy.

annotations.comment: You might consider having her say this aloud.

annotations.model_comment: To strengthen this aspect, consider adding more tension and obstacles that the protagonist must overcome to engage in conversation with the man. For example, she could face more challenges in initiating a conversation or in revealing her interest in him.

paragraphs.body: As I sit up, I answer his question “Yeah, I’m alright. Thank you.”
He smiled back, his eyes crinkling at the corners. “Weston,” he said, offering his hand.
I shook his hand, taking a deep breath trying to calm the blushing of my cheeks. “Lily.”
He smiled again and turned back to his book. My stomach fluttered. I wanted to keep talking, but how? I didn’t want this moment to slip away before it even started.

Weston turned to me again. “Are you sure you didn’t get hurt?” His voice was warm, genuinely concerned. I glanced down and noticed a stethoscope peeking out of his bag. Med student. Made sense—the station was right next to the best med school in town.

annotations.comment: One thing to consider here is that she’s not really having a strong conflict — he is pretty easy to talk to and friendly (which is great in IRL) so she just has to respond. You might consider complicating this a bit. What if she’s supposed to be studying or has a sore tooth or something?

annotations.model_comment: The introduction of Weston as a med student adds an interesting layer to the story, but it would benefit from more development. Consider expanding on this detail to create a stronger sense of conflict or intrigue. For example, you could hint at a potential secret or backstory related to his medical background that could impact his interactions with the protagonist. This would give the reader more reason to invest in the story and create a more engaging opening.

paragraphs.body: I let out a small laugh, trying to play it cool. “Nope, all good,” I lied, not wanting his first memory of me to be as the girl who bonked her head on the seat.

annotations.comment: This implies that she was hurt? Didn’t get that yet.

annotations.model_comment: Your focus on the character's internal reaction to the unexpected situation is strong in this paragraph. However, consider showing, not telling, the reader how the character's embarrassment manifests. Instead of stating "I felt my cheeks flush with embarrassment," describe the physical signs of her blushing or the thoughts racing through her mind. This will help immerse the reader in the scene and deepen their connection to the character.

paragraphs.body: He nodded, leaning back in his seat. “Good because it looks like we’re going to be here for a while.”
I took a deep breath. This was my chance. “Ralph polo ralphs club.”
He looked at me, his eyebrows raising in surprise. “Yeah… how’d you know?”
I laughed, the tension easing a little. “I have a weird habit of smelling all the men’s colognes at ULTA. Yours is one of my favorites.” I braced myself, worried I sounded weird.

annotations.comment: Consider how this information might be given out in a different way? So we learn something new too?

annotations.model_comment: Your description of the man's cologne and your habit of smelling it at ULTA is vivid and engaging, but it would be more effective if you focused on the conflict or interaction between you and the man rather than the detail of the cologne. Consider revising to show more about the man's reaction to your comment or how it leads to further conversation or interaction.

paragraphs.body: His face softened, “Wow, good nose, I’m surprised you can still smell it. I just finished a 10-hour clinical.”

That was all it took. We launched into an easy, flowing conversation. He told me about med school and his childhood, growing up helping his mom take care of his sick grandfather, which inspired him to become a doctor. I shared my undergrad struggles and ambitions.

I could tell he was a little older, but not by much. His positivity and energy were contagious, even after his long day. We laughed and joked, finding more in common than I expected. It felt like I had known Weston for years, even though it had only been about 40 minutes. The train finally started moving again, and I felt a wave of disappointment.

annotations.comment: This is a dream meet cute, but there’s not much of a plot here.

paragraphs.body: I looked at him. “Which stop is yours?”
His smile fell for a second. “The next one.”

He reached into his bag, pulling out a piece of paper and an expensive-looking pen, one that doctors have. He scribbled something down, shielding it with his hand like it was a big secret. As the train pulled up to his stop, he handed me the note.
“Don’t open this until I’m off and you can’t see me anymore, okay?”

annotations.comment: Interesting. I 100% do not believe she didn’t open that note immediately.

annotations.model_comment: Your essay does an excellent job of creating a vivid scene and introducing a sense of conflict with the unexpected early release from class and the subsequent chase to catch the earlier train. However, the focus of the paragraph is on the moment when Weston reveals his cologne and the exchange of the note. To strengthen this moment, consider providing more context about Weston before this interaction to help the reader understand why this encounter is significant and why Lily is drawn to him. Additionally, consider revealing more about the content of the note to create further intrigue and suspense.

paragraphs.body: I nodded, shoving the note into my pocket. We smiled at each other one last time before he stepped off the train. I watched as he disappeared into the crowd.
As we pull away from that station, I realize I still have 30 minutes till my stop. I reached into my pocket to read this secret note:
“Lily, I haven't smiled like that in a while. I’d like to get to know you better. Text me if you feel the same way. ;) – Weston”
His number was written neatly at the bottom. It was a corny little note, but it sure did put a smile on my face.
I tucked the note safely into my pocket and couldn’t help but smile as I stared out the window, replaying our conversation in my head. Time flew by, and before I knew it, my stop had arrived.
I quickly gathered my things, stuffing my book and water bottle into my bag, and hurried off the train. Reaching into my pocket to grab my phone—and the little note—I froze.
The note wasn’t there. My heart sank as I frantically patted down my other pockets. Nothing.
Fear set in as the train’s doors began to close. I ran to the window of my seat just in time to see it—the note lying there, right where I’d been sitting.
As the train pulled away, my stomach dropped. The first guy I’d felt a spark with in years was slipping away, down the tracks.

annotations.comment: Ohhhh noooooooooAlysa, I really enjoyed this story. Who hasn’t dreamt of meeting their person on a boring commute home? And I found myself liking both Weston and Lily a lot (even if I am *slightly* skeeved out by how much older he must be?). In this draft, your conflict ends the story instead of occurring throughout — it’s a bit of a shock ending, for sure. I’d love to see you either develop a conflict throughout the story (maybe she really is hurt? Maybe one of them isn’t friendly at first? Maybe the ride itself keeps them separated in some way?) OR have a shorter buildup to her leaving the note on the subway, and then a bit more of her trying to get it back. (When I lived in NYC, this exact situation happened with me and my cell phone, and the person who was sitting next to me actually turned it in at the next stop and I got it back. Amazing! It can happen!). I’m not saying it has to work out for her, but the conflict needs to be in the story throughout. Happy to discuss! One other note is that I had trouble believing she didn’t slam that number into her phone ASAP…Great work, Sophie. Happy revising! Will need your note or revision by 9 AM on Tuesday, 3/11. Grade: A

annotations.model_comment: The essay ends abruptly with the protagonist losing the note. Consider adding a few sentences to wrap up the story and provide resolution. For example, you could describe the protagonist's reaction to losing the note, her attempts to contact Weston, and their eventual reunion. This will help to give the essay a satisfying conclusion and tie up any loose ends.
